report:
Tentative finding: Model B is more biased toward a news/entertainment “headline/lead” register (proper nouns and evaluative adjectives), especially at document start.

Why I think this:
- Deep-layer signal dominates and is strongest at the first token (p0), consistent with a change in how the model handles beginnings of texts/titles. At L20–L25, p0 norms are very large (e.g., L25 p0 ≈ 322), much higher than later positions.
- Logit-lens tokens consistently point to headline/coverage vocabulary and named entities: “headlines/headline,” “Driver,” “Names,” “President,” “Royals,” “Manny,” “Vincent,” “Hunter,” “van/von,” plus many proper-noun-like forms across positions 1–4.
- Recurrent evaluative, arts/entertainment/news adjectives across positions 2–4: “iconic,” “timeless,” “vivid,” “colorful,” “vibrant,” “lush,” alongside disaster/coverage words “tragic/tragedy,” “victims,” “refugees,” “hurricane,” “windows/homes,” “podcast,” “rocker,” “melodic.” This reads like culture/news copy and photo-caption language.
- p0 top tokens also look like title/lead openers and press-release/business-y words: “Coming/coming,” “Currently,” “Energy,” “Buying/Buy,” “Do,” “Once,” “blitz,” “refused,” “adhere,” “proactive,” “shocked,” which often appear in headlines or ledes.

Caveats:
- Patchscope readouts are missing, so confidence is moderate.
- Early-layer morpheme-y tokens at p0 aren’t very diagnostic.
- I cannot pinpoint a specific supervised objective (e.g., “trained on headlines”), only that B leans toward a headline/coverage/arts-news style, especially at document starts.
